name: Classic physique division

card.summary: A bodybuilding division that judges symmetry, proportion and a small waist over sheer mass, giving competitors an aesthetic, V-tapered physique to build toward.
card.note: Competition prep involves extreme dieting and dehydration; performance-enhancing drug use is discussed in the sport.

quick.overview:
Classic Physique is a competitive bodybuilding division, introduced at the Mr. Olympia in 2016, that rewards symmetry, proportion, pleasing lines and a small waist rather than maximal size.[1] It sits between Open bodybuilding and Men's Physique.[2]

For people interested in looks, it offers a defined aesthetic target: broad shoulders, a tapered torso and balanced muscle. Research on the division covers coaching practices, peak-week methods and posing.
quick.how: Competitors train for balanced muscle development and diet for months before a show, with a final peaking phase that manipulates carbohydrate and water.[3] Posing, including the vacuum pose that shows a tapered torso, is judged alongside the physique.[2]
quick.risks: Contest prep involves extreme leanness and acute dehydration and carbohydrate manipulation.[3] Coaches in these divisions also report recommendations of performance-enhancing drugs at times.[4]

lead: The Classic Physique division is a men's bodybuilding class that emphasises symmetry, proportion, pleasing lines and a small waist over size and mass.[1] It debuted at the Mr. Olympia in 2016 with Danny Hester as its first champion, and Chris Bumstead won a record six consecutive titles from 2019 to 2024.[1]

In the sport's classification it sits between Open bodybuilding and Men's Physique, which was introduced in 2013 and uses board shorts.[2] Classic competitors wear trunks that show the legs.[2] Fans on forums often compare the division to the golden-age physiques of earlier decades.[5]

chain: Train for balanced muscle and a small waist
angle.text: The division defines an aesthetic ideal of proportion and taper. People aiming for that look train and diet toward it, whether or not they compete.

paras: Bodybuilding judges rank conditioning, muscularity, posing, size, stage presentation and symmetry, with mandatory poses followed by a routine.[2] Classic Physique weights symmetry and waist more than raw mass.[1]

Peak-week carbohydrate manipulation is common in bodybuilding and classic physique to raise glycogen and water in muscle before stage time.[6] A 2025 survey of 154 competitive physique athletes quantified weekly training volume per muscle group.[7] A qualitative study of coaches in these divisions looked at the decisions and rationales behind nutrition, training, supplement and drug recommendations.[4]

No clinical trials of the division itself exist. Observational studies include a 2024 analysis of posing in Mr. Olympia Classic Physique athletes (2016-2023), which found a general rightward bias in mandatory poses.[8]

timeline.event: Classic Physique debuts at Mr. Olympia.[1]
Chris Bumstead begins six straight wins.[1]
